Path.notes: The signal input and the four outputs carry whatever you patch in, so they are given no family. sumRange for the ROUTE CV input is written as a voltage range because the field takes only those four spellings; the quantity it clamps is the 0-to-1 routing position, not a voltage. Fuji.notes: The maker's second line on gate inputs 2 to 6 says each is normalled to the gate input for the channel above, and the code bears it out. The maker's second line on every mode switch describes the two modes: an AD envelope on each gate or trigger in Attack Decay mode, and a peak held for the length of the gate in Hold mode. Attack and decay run 1.5ms to 1.5 seconds on a base-10 knob, with an empirical 0.5 scale factor applied before the slew limiter; the maker's comment calls the times characteristic rather than exact. The gate inputs use Rack's default Schmitt thresholds of 0.1V and 1V. A looping channel's output swings ±8V; a one-shot channel's is clamped to 0-8V.

Sena.notes: The frequency ranges are literals in the source: VCO coarse 15Hz to 1000Hz, LFO coarse 0.15Hz to 10Hz, and both fine ranges a twelfth of a semitone either side of C0 at 16.352Hz (src/Sena.cpp:210-221). Linear FM adds 120 times the input voltage in hertz and is DC blocked. Switching a channel to fine tuning resets its frequency knob to the middle of that range (src/Sena.cpp:525-528), which is a real jump in pitch and is not documented by the maker. The channel 4 mod input behaves differently from the other three: the PWM knob scales the incoming CV rather than offsetting it (src/Sena.cpp:586-587). sumRange on the mod inputs is written as a voltage range because the field takes only those four spellings; the quantity clamped is the 0-to-1 shaping amount. The noise generators use random::normal rather than a bounded uniform, so their peaks are not hard limited.

Hive.notes: The maker's second line on the four pan CV inputs reads '5Vp-p bipolar CV for panning, sums with the pan knob'; the code divides the input by 2.5, so ±2.5V is the full sweep, which is 5V peak to peak as the maker says. The pan law is the maker's own, square-root times linear, giving about 1.5dB of centre attenuation. Chaining works only in one direction: a Hive passes its mix to the Hive on its right, and only when its own two outputs are unpatched (src/Hive.cpp:164-173). The chain shows itself as a menu label reading that the module is chained to the Hive on its left, which is a label rather than an item and so is not written as a menu line.

Halo.notes: The panel draws the maker's normalling arrow beside the frequency input column, as Asset, Ceres, Fuji, Atlas and Sena all do, but Halo's process reads those inputs with a plain getVoltage and never carries a value forward (src/Halo.cpp:74-75). The frequency input line names that conflict. The logic is done on the analogue waveforms rather than on gates: AND is the sample-by-sample minimum, OR the maximum, XOR the maximum less the minimum, and MIX their average, so all four outputs are continuous voltages rather than gates. sumRange on the frequency inputs is written as a voltage range because the field takes only those four spellings; the quantity clamped is the 0-to-1 knob position. The frequency ranges are literals: 0.00875Hz to 8.75Hz in LO and 0.05Hz to 87.5Hz in HI.
